title: Unaligned Image Guided Denoising via Cross-modal Conditional Flow Matching
claim: Restoration unfolds progressively along a trajectory, where cleaner images and better-aligned guidance mutually reinforce each other over time.
layout: Top timeline left-to-right, two bottom boxes zoomed from early and late stages
description: A horizontal timeline runs across the top, titled 'Conditional Flow Matching Trajectory'. On the left, a noisy RGB image and an unaligned NIR image feed through black connector lines into a circle marked t→0. A gradient arrow runs from blue to pink to orange, through a circle marked t→1, and ends at the clean RGB target image on the right. Below the arrow, two small images are labeled 'Highly corrupted stage' and 'Relatively cleaner stage'. Dashed arrows point from the two circles to two rounded boxes at the bottom. The blue box (early) and the orange box (late) each show a heatmap of aligned guidance features and a denoised image. Each has blue and red zoom-in patches that show the guidance becoming sharper and the image cleaner at the late stage. Blue and orange colors separate early from late.
caption: Illustration of the cross-modal conditional flow matching trajectory of UGD-FM. Given a noisy RGB image and an unaligned NIR guidance image, UGD-FM progressively restores the RGB state toward the clean target, forming a mutual reinforcing process between image restoration and guidance aggregation. For clearer visualization, the brightness of the zoom-in patches is enhanced.
abstract: This work presents UGD-FM, a novel unaligned image guided denoising framework based on cross-modal conditional flow matching. Unlike previous approaches that assume spatially aligned inputs or only handle small-baseline rectified pairs, we address a more challenging setting where severe target noise and large-range two-dimensional cross-modal misalignment coexist. Specifically, we formulate guided denoising as a progressive flow matching process, allowing image restoration and aligned guidance aggregation to mutually reinforce each other. To support efficient few-step inference, we introduce a stage-focused and inference-consistent training strategy that focuses on task-critical denoising stages, and mitigates the training-inference mismatch. We further propose adaptive sparse guidance propagation for efficient and reliable large-range matching, regularized by perceptual and geometric auxiliary losses. Experiments demonstrate that UGD-FM achieves state-of-the-art denoising performance with only one or two inference steps, and is compatible with modern single-image restoration backbones.
